title: On The Hook React Native customer mobile app
description: Implement the full v1 On The Hook Fish & Chips customer app for iOS and Android from one React Native codebase, following the packaged design/content/API/test specifications. The app prioritizes finding upcoming trucks, menu/about information, and optional visit notifications. Ordering remains an external handoff.
acceptance_criteria:
- All child beads are complete and closed.
- iOS and Android builds pass the release gate in specs/TEST_PLAN.md.
- No runtime website HTML scraping, native ordering/cart/checkout, or mandatory account flow exists.
- Official first-party production logo art replaces the packaged reference logo before store release.
notes: All children are now closed, deferred, or blocked. Remaining blockers are external: first-party production API/push scheduler, approved official brand masters, map/calendar implementation decisions, and macOS iOS device/simulator validation.

title: Build Find Us map mode with synchronized selection
description: Add list/map toggle and interactive map for the current result set. Map mode must use event coordinates supplied by the API and synchronize selected events with list/detail navigation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Only valid-coordinate events receive markers.
- Viewport fits result markers without excessive world-scale zoom.
- Selected marker opens a compact card/bottom sheet with event summary and actions.
- Switching from a selected list event to map centers/selects that event when coordinates exist.
- Map handles zero-coordinate results with a useful explanation/list fallback.
- No bulk client-side address geocoding is performed.
notes: Blocked: no approved map SDK/provider, API key configuration, or valid-coordinate fixture coverage is present. The app must not geocode client-side as a substitute.

title: Implement push device registration API
description: Implement POST/PUT/DELETE push device endpoints from API_CONTRACT.md in the first-party backend. Use installation/device identifiers rather than customer accounts; securely persist registration state and suppress token logging.
acceptance_criteria:
- Device registration accepts platform, opaque push token, app version, locale, and timezone.
- Preferences can be created/updated idempotently.
- Delete removes or disables device subscription.
- Raw push tokens are excluded from logs and analytics.
- Backend tests cover duplicate registration/token rotation and invalid input.
notes: Blocked: this workspace has only the React Native client and no backend service, database, scheduler host, or deployment configuration in which to implement and test the specified POST/PUT/DELETE endpoints.

title: Implement mobile push registration and preference sync
description: Implement iOS APNs/Android FCM registration through a shared push adapter. After user-granted permission, register token with the first-party backend and synchronize home-area/alert preferences. Handle token rotation and logout-free reinstall semantics via installationId.
acceptance_criteria:
- Push token is requested/registered only after OS permission is granted.
- Token rotation updates backend registration.
- Preferences retry safely after transient failures.
- Disabling alerts removes/deactivates backend registration as specified.
- No raw token is logged or sent to analytics.
- iOS and Android adapters expose a consistent typed interface.
notes: Blocked by the absent first-party push device API (oth-mobile.25); no push token provider or backend device registration endpoint exists in this mobile-only workspace.

title: Implement server-side truck-visit notification scheduler
description: Implement the scheduled backend process that matches upcoming truck visits to home-area subscriptions and sends selected push alert types. Use idempotency and event-local timezone behavior. Do not require continuous device location.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduled-nearby alert is emitted once per device/event when a newly relevant visit appears.
- Day-before and morning-of alerts respect event-local timezone and user preference.
- Idempotency key prevents duplicates across scheduler retries/feed refreshes.
- Canceled events suppress unsent alerts; reschedules use updated timing without duplicating already-sent alert type.
- Invalid push tokens are disabled/cleaned up.
- Backend tests cover duplicate, canceled, rescheduled, timezone, and preference cases.
notes: Blocked: requires the absent server-side push device store, scheduler host, and push-provider credentials. It cannot be safely implemented in the mobile-only workspace.

title: Build Notification Settings screen
description: Provide post-onboarding settings for OS permission status, home area, alert switches, enable/disable flow, and a link to system settings when permission is denied/restricted.
acceptance_criteria:
- Settings reflect real OS permission state and backend-synced preferences.
- Changing home area or switches updates backend idempotently.
- Disable alerts stops future push delivery and updates local state.
- Denied permission state does not repeatedly prompt; it links to OS settings.
- Screen works after app reinstall/registration recreation.
notes: Blocked by mobile push synchronization (oth-mobile.26). The pre-permission UI exists, but backend-synced settings and disable registration cannot be implemented without the missing API.

title: Accessibility pass for iOS VoiceOver
description: Perform an end-to-end accessibility implementation pass for all v1 screens and shared controls.
acceptance_criteria:
• All interactive controls expose meaningful labels/roles/states.
• External links announce that they leave the app.
• Map markers have accessible equivalents through the list; discovery never requires interacting with the map.
• Dynamic Type/font scaling does not clip primary actions.
• Color contrast meets intended WCAG AA target for text/control states.
• Reduce Motion is honored.
• Manual VoiceOver test checklist is completed.
notes: Blocked pending completion of all screens and manual VoiceOver/Reduce Motion validation on an iOS Simulator or device, which requires the macOS/Xcode environment.

title: Implement privacy-conscious analytics taxonomy
description: Implement the event taxonomy in specs/ANALYTICS.md through the repository analytics abstraction. If no analytics provider is configured, provide a no-op adapter rather than blocking app functionality.
acceptance_criteria:
- Core navigation, discovery, directions, calendar, order handoff, menu category, notification setup, external links, offline cache, and API failure events are instrumented.
- No precise coordinates, push tokens, email/phone, raw free-text search, or full orderUrl are emitted.
- Analytics implementation can be disabled/no-op without feature code changes.
- Automated tests verify sensitive fields are absent from payloads.
notes: Blocked from final acceptance until unavailable map/calendar/push features exist; implemented no-op privacy-filtered taxonomy covers available app, discovery, directions, menu, notification, external, and order events.

title: Configure iOS app capabilities permissions and branding
description: Configure the iOS target: bundle identifier/config, location-when-in-use usage description, notification capability, APNs environment, calendar usage strings/entitlements as required by the chosen calendar library, URL schemes/deep links, icons/splash from official brand masters, and release signing strategy.
acceptance_criteria:
- iOS app launches on supported simulator/device.
- Only foreground location permission is declared.
- Notification permission/capability works with dev and production configuration separated.
- Calendar permission wording is contextual/accurate.
- App icons/splash use approved official brand art before release.
- Info.plist privacy strings match actual behavior.
notes: Blocked pending approved official logo/icon/splash master, calendar implementation decision, and APNs backend/push registration configuration. Current Info.plist only declares foreground location.

title: Configure Android app capabilities permissions and branding
description: Configure Android package/app, notification permission/version handling, foreground location permission, maps configuration, calendar intent/API behavior, deep links, adaptive icon/splash from official brand masters, and FCM production/staging separation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Android app launches on supported emulator/device.
- No background location permission is declared.
- Android 13+ notification permission behavior is handled.
- Maps and FCM configuration are environment-safe and keys are not committed.
- Adaptive icon/splash use approved official brand art before release.
- Manifest contains only permissions required by implemented features.
notes: Android work is paused; defer Android-specific native configuration and cross-platform parity until it resumes.

title: Performance and image optimization pass
description: Profile startup, scrolling, map/list switching, image decoding, network churn, and memory usage on representative iOS/Android devices/emulators. Optimize without degrading brand fidelity.
acceptance_criteria:
- Find Us remains responsive with 250 event fixtures.
- List rows avoid unnecessary re-renders and are virtualized.
- Images use appropriate dimensions/compression for rendered size.
- No synchronous bulk geocoding exists.
- Map markers do not cause severe frame drops for normal schedule sizes.
- No runaway polling/background tasks are present.
notes: Blocked pending instrumented iOS device/simulator profiling and map implementation; photo resizing is complete but end-to-end performance targets require Xcode tooling.

title: Final visual polish and cross-platform parity pass
description: Compare all screens against specs/DESIGN.md on narrow/standard/large iPhones and representative Android widths. Correct spacing, typography, safe-area, keyboard, image cropping, tab behavior, and platform-specific interaction inconsistencies.
acceptance_criteria:
- Home/Find Us/Menu/More feel visually coherent and branded.
- No clipped text or unreachable actions at target widths/font sizes.
- Safe areas and Android edge-to-edge insets are correct.
- External-link indicators and button hierarchy are consistent.
- Decorative assets are used sparingly and do not make screens visually noisy.
- Shared behavior is functionally equivalent on iOS and Android.
notes: Android work is paused; defer Android-specific native configuration and cross-platform parity until it resumes.
